arguments.heading: Argument session of April 20, 2026
paragraphs: The the side that brought the case asked the Court to reverse. Ms. Prelogar argued the suit is a collateral attack, not an appeal, and that district courts lack appellate jurisdiction over state judgments.

The justices tested several assumptions. Justice Thomas probed appellate jurisdiction and agency-versus-judgment review. Justice Sotomayor tested what voiding means. Justice Jackson tested reconsidering Rooker-Feldman, and Justice Alito tested overruling it without a request. No reargument occurred in this session.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case involves a rule called Rooker-Feldman. It means federal district courts generally cannot overturn a state court judgment. The question is how far that rule reaches.
The approved record does not support a detailed description of the underlying dispute, so this summary sticks to what the argument transcript shows.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: Chief Justice Roberts opened the session and recognized the Solicitor General's counsel for the the side that brought the case. The argument began at 11:16 a.m.
After the main argument, the Chief Justice called for rebuttal. Ms. Prelogar then presented rebuttal for the the side that brought the case.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The the side that brought the case asked the Court to reverse the lower court's decision. Ms. Prelogar made that request at the close of her argument.
The approved record does not describe a separate requested result for the other side. The transcript does not support adding one here.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The the side that brought the case conceded the suit is a collateral attack on the state court judgment. She kept the point that it differs from an appeal.
She explained that collateral attacks are new cases. They can involve new evidence, cannot vacate the state judgment, and face preclusion defenses.
She also said district courts can only exercise original jurisdiction, not appellate jurisdiction. The approved record does not include the other side's argument claims.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Thomas asked whether a district court has appellate jurisdiction. He also asked about differences between reviewing an agency decision and a court judgment.
Justice Sotomayor clarified what the other side meant by review and reject. She identified the relief as voiding the judgment or declaring it unconstitutional.
Justice Jackson asked about reconsidering Rooker-Feldman as a backup. Justice Alito questioned overruling it when the petition did not request that.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The the side that brought the case's answers show the stakes. A district court cannot vacate or revise a state judgment in a collateral challenge.
Remedies stay limited to declarations or injunctions controlling the parties before the court. That shapes what relief litigants can seek.
